meta_title: Areca CMS: the open-source, self-hosted CMS for agencies
meta_description: Areca CMS is an MIT-licensed, self-hosted CMS for agency-run websites. Clients write and approve; releases are frozen snapshots your site pulls at build time.
hero_lead: Areca CMS is the open-source CMS for agencies. Your clients write and approve. You ship. Every release is a frozen snapshot your site pulls at build time, so published pages never call home.
hero_note: Free and MIT licensed. Runs on your own server.
hero_video_label: A short loop of the Areca editor, recorded on the live demo.
video_caption: Recorded on the real CMS and the Northbound Coffee demo site.
how_lead: Areca separates writing from publishing. Nothing reaches visitors until someone approves it and a release is built.
how_step1_body: Editors write drafts in a calm canvas editor. Drafts never touch the live site.
how_step2_body: An owner marks the entry ready. Ready means approved for the next release, not live.
how_step3_body: One click freezes every ready change into an immutable snapshot with a checksum.
how_step4_body: Your site's build runs areca pull. Content becomes JSON files and images land in your public folder.
how_step5_body: The build deploys as plain files. Areca waits until the site reports that exact release before calling it live.
how_art_label: Animation: an entry moves from draft, to ready, to a frozen snapshot, is pulled into the site build, and is served as static files.
home_title: The CMS your website never calls.
home_lead: Most headless CMSs sit on your site's critical path: every page view or rebuild asks their API for content. Areca steps out of the way. At build time, areca pull writes the published snapshot into your project and downloads every image next to it. What ships is plain files.
home_typical_caption: Every visit depends on the CMS API being up, fast and within quota.
home_areca_caption: Visitors get static files. The CMS only speaks up when you build.
home_art_label: Animation comparing a typical headless CMS, which answers a request for every visitor, with Areca, which only sends content to the site at build time.
home_point1_body: Take the CMS down for an upgrade. Your sites don't notice.
home_point2_body: Keep the CMS behind a VPN or firewall. Visitors never reach it.
home_point3_body: No API quotas, no cold starts, no per-request bill.
home_point4_body: Every release is kept. Restoring one rebuilds the site from that exact snapshot.
home_footnote: Draft previews are the one exception: they ask the CMS for unpublished content with a signed token that expires within the hour.
features_title: An editor your clients will actually like
features_lead: Areca is built for the people who write, not the people who configure. Pick a feature to see it in the real CMS.
zoom_open: Open the screenshot full screen to zoom in
zoom_hint: Scroll or pinch to zoom. Drag to move around. Double-click to toggle.
feature_editor_body: The title is the page. Rich text with headings, tables, images and highlighted code. Autosave, revision history and crash recovery are built in.
feature_visual_title: See the page while you type
feature_visual_body: A live preview of the real site sits beside the fields. Click a heading or a price on the page and Areca jumps to the field behind it.
feature_languages_body: Translate field by field with the main language in view, or let AI fill the empty fields for you to review. Each language gets its own URL.
feature_seo_title: Ready for search and answer engines
feature_seo_body: Titles, descriptions, FAQs, key takeaways and JSON-LD for every entry. AI drafts them from your content, and nothing applies until you pick it.
feature_releases_body: See exactly what is changing, follow the build as it runs, and roll back to any earlier release.
feature_library_body: Images and files are shared across a client's sites, with missing-description filters and protection for files still in use.

feature_shot_alt_visual: The visual editor: fields on the left, a live preview of the coffee shop site on the right.

agency_title: Built for the way agencies work
agency_lead: One installation runs every client. Each client has its own sites, people and library, and you switch between them in a keystroke.
agency_art_label: Diagram: one agency with several clients, each with their own sites and people.
agency_point1_body: Editors write. Owners approve and go live. Agency admins manage everything else.
agency_point2_body: Set the name, logo, colour and font. The sign-in page and every email follow.
agency_point3_body: Two-factor sign-in for admins, a fresh code for sensitive actions, and an activity log for every change.
agency_point4_body: Give any site a throwaway copy for schema work, then push the changes you choose to production.
agency_shot_alt: The agency overview listing every client site and what needs attention.
ai_lead: Every site has its own MCP server. Connect Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or VS Code and your assistant can draft, translate and upload with exactly the permissions of the person who connected it.
ai_point1: Drafts stay drafts until a person approves them.
ai_point2: Editors' assistants can't publish. Owners' assistants go live only when asked.
ai_point3: Every change made through AI shows up in the activity log.
ai_skills_body: One command teaches your coding agent the SDK, the content model and the release flow.
ai_art_label: Animation: a chat message asks for a new coffee page, the assistant creates a draft, and the draft waits for an owner's approval.
ai_art_prompt: Add our new Panama Geisha to the shop, in English and Dutch.
dev_title: Typed content, no CMS at runtime
dev_lead: Define your content model in code, pull the published snapshot at build time, and read it with full types. Your site ships without a CMS client.
dev_point1: Schema lives in areca.config.ts and is pushed with one command.
dev_point2: Twelve field types, from rich text and images to references and dates.
dev_point3: Generated types for every collection and field. No generics to wire up.
dev_point4: Framework-agnostic: TanStack Start, Next.js, Astro, SvelteKit or plain Node.
dev_visual_body: Spread field() on an element and editors can click it in the live preview to jump straight to that field.
dev_art_label: Animation: a cursor clicks a heading in the site preview and the matching field in the editor is highlighted.
host_lead: Areca runs anywhere Docker runs. The Compose file starts the CMS with PostgreSQL, Redis and S3-compatible storage. Open /setup to create the first admin.
host_point1: Builds your sites on Dokploy or Cloudflare Pages and Workers.
host_point2: No telemetry, no licence keys, no phoning home.
host_point3: Backups are a Postgres dump and your storage bucket.
oss_body: The CMS, the site SDK and the agent skills are all MIT. Read the code, run it anywhere, change what you need. There is no paid tier holding features back.
faq_q1: Is Areca a static site generator?
faq_a1: No. Areca is the CMS. Your site keeps its own framework and build, and reads content from files that areca pull writes into the project.
faq_q2: Do I need to rebuild to publish?
faq_a2: Yes. Go live builds your site with the new snapshot. That build step is what makes published pages independent of the CMS.
faq_q3: Can editors preview drafts before they go live?
faq_a3: Yes. Previews use a signed, short-lived token, and the visual editor shows unsaved changes as you type.
faq_q4: What does it need to run?
faq_a4: Node, PostgreSQL, Redis and S3-compatible storage. The Docker Compose file in the repository starts all of them.
faq_q5: Where can my sites be hosted?
faq_a5: Areca triggers builds through Dokploy or Cloudflare Pages and Workers. The output is static files, so the site itself is fast and cheap to serve.
faq_a6: Yes. Areca is MIT licensed and self-hosted. There is no paid edition.
